title: A student day and household jobs
instructions: Read the three short profiles. Complete the language and detail questions in order. This is foundation language practice, not an IELTS Reading section.

stimulus.text:
A. Dan is a university student in the source example. His day begins at eight with a shower and breakfast. Before going to lectures, he gets his books ready. His lectures continue until midday. He generally returns home and prepares lunch around twelve thirty. Sometimes he watches television afterwards. Around three he often meets a friend for coffee. Half an hour later they go to the library. He studies there for several hours before returning home around six thirty. He usually makes dinner for himself and the other people in his flat. Later he may exercise or see friends, and usually falls asleep near midnight.

B. Another household description divides jobs among family members. The narrator usually helps the mother do the laundry and always puts the bedroom in order after school. The brother does not wash his clothes: he leaves them on the bedroom floor. Sometimes he takes the rubbish outside, but often leaves it by the back door instead of carrying it to the bins. The father sometimes washes dishes because the dishwasher has broken. The sister enjoys cooking and helps prepare meals. After the housework, the family relaxes and watches television together.

questions.prompt: Complete using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from A: Dan gets his ______ ready before lectures.
Which phrase in B means “wash clothes”?
Complete using ONE WORD from A: After coffee Dan goes to the ______.
Choose the correct form: Dan usually ______ dinner for his flatmates.
Which description matches the brother in B?

options.text: He always takes rubbish to the bins.
He sometimes moves it outside but often leaves it by the back door.

questions.prompt: Complete using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from B: The dishwasher has ______.
Which sentence preserves the frequency in A?

options.text: Dan has coffee with a friend often, not necessarily every day.
Dan always has coffee at midnight.

criteria.label: Textual evidence
criteria.description: Select or supply the answer warranted by this passage, observing the response limit and distinction between contradiction and absence.

answerKey.rationale: A states he gets his books ready.
B uses do the laundry for washing clothes; the alternatives concern tidying or rubbish.
B assigns dishwashing to the father.
A gives the library after the three o’clock coffee.
A describes his regular meal preparation; third-person simple-present makes is required.
B qualifies the rubbish activity and says he does not wash his clothes.
B gives the broken dishwasher as the reason for hand-washing dishes.
A says often meets a friend around three, not always or never.

assessment.feedbackGuidance: After submission, use each explicit profile rationale. Separate an incorrect verb form, misunderstood frequency word, confused person/time/direction and copying/limit error. Model one correction using another original sentence: “She cycles; they cycle.” Then ask for a corrected answer and one new routine sentence. Raw practice accuracy is not a band or proof of A 2 mastery.
